messages:
maria: quick recap — per the RFC follow-up, we need to decide whether the dashboard should call the query layer with a flattened 'render spec' (single endpoint returns assembled tiles) or keep tile composition client-side and fetch raw slices. tradeoffs: RBAC enforcement consistency vs network roundtrips and SLO exposure. asking for quick thumbs + a concrete preference by EOD :hourglass:

devin: my leaning is server-side composition (flattened render spec). single call = easier to reason about tail latency and we can enforce auth once in the execution path. also easier to attach tracing for cost attribution. :+1:

liam: worried about the cost/compute surface. server-side composition can blow up GPU/CPU if dashboards are high-cardinality. we'd need a cap/budget layer or partial materialization to avoid snowballing costs.

sasha: what about a hybrid? compose small common tiles server-side, let client do fanout for heavy/rare slices. we can codify that as a policy in the routing layer. minimal changes to RBAC since server-side still authorizes the primary call.

maria: hybrid seems attractive. specifics: define a "surface contract" where endpoint returns metadata about tile locality and gated prefetch hints. client can request heavy tiles separately. thoughts on what that contract looks like?

devin: sketch: response = { status, tiles: [{id, ready, auth_token_hint, weight_estimate}], prefetch_hint: [ids] }. sample: ```json\n{\n  \"tiles\": [{\"id\":\"t1\",\"ready\":true,\"weight\":12}, {\"id\":\"t2\",\"ready\":false}],\n  \"prefetch_hint\": [\"t2\"]\n}\n```

liam: auth_token_hint worries me — we must not leak tokens. better to return capability scopes (strings) and let the client call the control-plane to mint one-time capability if needed. that keeps audit logs central.

sasha: agree on capability scopes. also we should add a size/timeout budget per dashboard request, enforced by the query executor to protect SLOs. fallback path: return placeholders and a "retry-after" header for client to poll or lazy-load.

maria: sounds like a plan. actionables: 1) devex: write the surface contract proto + examples (devin) 2) infra: add budget/weight enforcement and telemetry (liam) 3) security: capability scope design + audit hooks (sasha) 4) product: pick defaults for prefetch window and tile weight (maria). aim for a prototype next sprint.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: new ticket created: CONSOLE-1298 - dashboard surface contract + hybrid composition prototype (assignee: devin) :ticket:

devin: one more note — metrics we should emit: per-request tile-count, server-composed-tokens, tail-99 latency, auth-eval-time. that'll help tune the budget.

liam: for the prototype I'll add a small simulator to replay real dashboard patterns and run cost/lambda estimates. will post results as a short gist.

maria: perfect. thanks everyone, we'll lock the RFC follow-up doc with these action items. :rocket:
